business_scope.primary_industry_name: Precision Heavy-Load Polymer-Modified Bitumen Runway Laying

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code; droit écrit with limited common-law influences in commercial practice)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 30 May 1984, entered into force 17 March 1985)
France-Germany Double Taxation Agreement (1959, as amended)
France-United States Double Taxation Convention (1994, as amended by 2006 and 2009 protocols)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (Articles 49 and 63 concerning freedom of establishment and capital movements)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Articles L561-1 to L561-58-2 implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; Decree No. 2016-1795 of 30 December 2016; Act No. 2018-134 of 23 March 2018; Decree No. 2018-936 of 29 October 2018 (UBO register); Decree No. 2019-1330 of 26 December 2019; Arrêté of 25 June 2019; UBO filing requirements under CMF Articles L561-46 to L561-52 and Code de commerce Articles R123-1 to R123-9.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport and proof of address for each natural-person shareholder and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or registered translator in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if the country of origin is a 1961 Hague Convention party), otherwise Consular Legalization at the French Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (attestation de non-insolvabilité) for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's state of incorporation (e.g., Companies House, UF-Net, Hong Kong Companies Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus French sworn translation (traduction assermentée)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association and current corporate extract (including UBO list) of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar or competent corporate body in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus French sworn translation (traduction assermentée)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (procuration) authorising the French avocat to undertake pre-incorporation formalities and incorporate the SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization) plus French sworn translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Domiciliation agreement or lease contract for the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French notary or authorised domiciliation company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No Apostille needed when issued in France; must be attested in French

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and senior managers against EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated list, French Direction Générale du Trésor sanctions, OFAC/SDN list (whenever the transaction involves USD or US nexus), and European/French PEP lists. Enhanced due diligence applies to non-resident PEPs under CMF Article L561-10-2. Screening is required before incorporation, at each AML trigger event, and at least annually.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) operated by INPI, accessed through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr or data.inpi.fr; RCS formalities are executed by the Greffes des tribunaux de commerce.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All statutory submissions and attachments must be in French. The corporate name (dénomination sociale) may use a foreign word or expression, but if the script is non-Latin (Chinese, Arabic, Greek, Cyrillic), an official French transliteration into Latin characters must be filed. The name must not create confusion with existing registered names under Code de commerce Article L123-9 and must not be contrary to public order or morality.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Banca / Credit – requires prior Banque de France or ACPR authorisation
Avocat / Notaire / Commissaire aux comptes – reserved to regulated legal professions
République / État / Ministre / Préfecture / Mairie / Gendarmerie – implies official capacity; requires ministerial consent
Aéroport / Aéronautique / Aviation – could mislead as to airport operator concession; requires DGAC prior consent if used in runway-related contracting
National / France / Français – may be refused if misleading as to state sponsorship
Chambre de Commerce / Bourse – reserved to public and regulatory institutions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RNE/INPI rejects the name application, the applicant may first file a corrective re-submission within 10 days of the refusal communication. If the refusal is final, a formal appeal (recours gracieux) may be lodged with the INPI within 2 months. Parallel use of a new name can be filed immediately. For conflicts with existing registered names, the founder or the avocat may bring a private action before the Tribunal de Commerce under Article L711-2 of the Intellectual Property Code and Article 1382 of the Civil Code. Where a violation of RNE procedure is alleged, an administrative appeal may be made to the Tribunal administratif de Paris within 2 months of the refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an SAS engaged in civil-aviation runway paving, a pure virtual office (domiciliation) is permissible only for the statutory registered address where the company also maintains a physical operational establishment in France. The DGAC and labour inspectorate require accessible premises, statutory files, and safety registers at an actual address. A virtual office alone will not satisfy the licence and commercial substance conditions for airport works under the French Aviation Code.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 35% annual probability for the registered office, and above 50% for airport construction sites, based on unannounced inspections by the Direction Générale de l'Aviation Civile (DGAC), the labour inspectorate (Inspection du travail), and tax/public auditors in consequence of non-resident ownership or unusual payment rails.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) / Guichet Unique

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS/immatriculation filing fees at the Greffe du tribunal de commerce (droit de greffe)

Domiciliation contract for the registered office of the SAS (first 12 months)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, including Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.227-1 to R.227-2 governing the Société par Actions Simplifiée; Articles L.123-1 et seq. governing the Trade and Companies Register; Articles L.123-11 et seq. governing registered offices; Articles L.561-46 and R.561-55 et seq. governing beneficial-owner declarations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent filing channel is the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI). The company is registered in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés by the competent commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce or designated commercial court registry) for the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic company-formation filing submitted through the Guichet unique, supported by signed SAS articles of association, the declaration of incorporation particulars, the beneficial-owner declaration, and the required supporting documents. The resulting registration certificate is the Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid at incorporation; the balance must be paid within five years of registration. Contributions in kind must be fully contributed at incorporation. Capital must be deposited with an authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts before filing, and the deposit certificate must be included. The amount stated is subject to applicable registry, beneficial-owner, and filing charges; the USD figure is an indicative conversion of the standard commercial registration charge and is not a fixed statutory USD tariff.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The President records that the Company has been duly incorporated as a société par actions simplifiée. It is resolved that the shareholders’ subscriptions and cash contributions be accepted and that the deposited funds be released to the Company’s bank account upon registration. The registered office is adopted at [full address], France. [Name] is appointed President for an unlimited term, and [Name] is appointed Directeur Général, if applicable, each accepting office and confirming eligibility. The officers are authorized to complete all registrations, beneficial-owner filings, bank formalities, tax registrations, insurance arrangements, and licensing applications required for the Company’s runway-paving activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm the corporate structure and prepare the SAS articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, operated by INPI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the corporate name, registered office, duration, corporate purpose, share capital, shareholder identity, share classes, transfer restrictions, governance rules, President, and any Directeur Général. Prepare and sign the SAS articles electronically or in wet ink. Ensure the corporate purpose covers airport runway paving, asphalt and bitumen handling, public works, equipment operation, subcontracting, and related activities.
required_dossiers: Officer identity and declaration of non-conviction and filiation
Registered-office title, lease, domiciliation agreement, or host-company attestation
Corporate certificates and powers of attorney for corporate shareholders
French translation by a sworn translator where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct defective articles, incomplete identity evidence, corporate-purpose ambiguity, or invalid powers of attorney and resubmit through the Guichet unique. Obtain an updated registered-office document where the registry challenges address availability.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the capital deposit account and pay in share subscriptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized French bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the draft articles, shareholder identification, subscription schedule, source-of-funds information, and proposed registered office to the depositary. Pay at least 50% of cash contributions into the temporary capital account. Obtain the certificate of deposit showing the amount, depositor, and intended SAS.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank KYC requests, correct subscriber information, or replace the depositary if the account cannot be opened. Do not file without a compliant capital-deposit certificate unless the filing is based solely on non-cash contributions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Journal of Legal Notices (Journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the statutory formation notice containing the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, President, and applicable transfer provisions. Use an authorized publication service and retain the publication certificate for the electronic filing.
required_dossiers: Publication certificate or attestation of notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction or republication if the notice contains a material error, particularly in the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, or officer identity. Upload the corrected certificate with the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the electronic formation and beneficial-owner filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises; underlying registry: competent commercial court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the electronic filing, select commercial company formation, upload the articles and all supporting documents, complete the beneficial-owner declaration, pay the applicable charges, and electronically sign the filing. Declare the principal activity as airport runway asphalt paving and related public-works contracting. Monitor the filing dashboard and retain the acknowledgment.
required_dossiers: Corporate shareholder documents and powers of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer registry queries within the stated deadline through the Guichet unique, upload corrected documents, and pay any additional charge. If rejected, identify the reason in the rejection notice, cure the defect, and resubmit or use the available registry appeal or judicial review route.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive registration evidence and complete post-incorporation records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent commercial court registry, INPI, tax administration, and social-security authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the registration certificate and Kbis extract when issued. Convert the temporary capital account into the operating account, record the share ledger and shareholder accounts, preserve the articles and formation evidence, and complete tax, payroll, employer, and beneficial-owner updates applicable to the business.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Escalate delayed issuance through the Guichet unique and the relevant registry. Correct post-registration discrepancies by filing a modification formalité and, where necessary, an amended beneficial-owner declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt governance controls and authorize regulated operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company President and shareholders; competent prefecture, airport operator, environmental authority, and occupational-safety bodies for operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first board or shareholder resolution required by the articles, appoint officers, approve banking powers, establish delegated signing limits, and adopt conflicts, procurement, health-and-safety, and document-retention controls. Before mobilization, verify airport access, works authorization, public-works insurance, environmental permissions, plant permits, waste arrangements, and aviation operational constraints.
required_dossiers: Professional civil-liability and ten-year construction insurance evidence where applicable
Airport works permit or contractual authorization
Environmental and ICPE records where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Suspend site mobilization until the missing authorization is obtained. Cure through the issuing airport operator, prefecture, environmental authority, insurer, or labor-safety body, and document the corrective action before restarting works.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: There is no single general French manufacturing license for runway paving contractors. The relevant authorities are the prefecture of the department, the Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL), the airport operator, and, for civil-aviation operational matters, the Direction générale de l'aviation civile (DGAC). An asphalt-mixing plant may require authorization, registration, or declaration under the Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE) regime.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Applicable title: ICPE authorization, ICPE registration, or ICPE declaration for an asphalt-mixing plant, principally under French Environmental Code nomenclature heading 2521, according to plant capacity and process. A runway-paving contractor without a separate fixed plant generally requires airport works authorization, contractual public-works approval, appropriate construction insurance, and site-specific environmental and safety clearances rather than a general operating license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition, implemented locally through the relevant prefecture and DREAL; environmental-authority opinions are issued under the French Environmental Code framework.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Case-specific screening. A project may require a full environmental impact assessment, a case-by-case examination, or no EIA depending on the works, airport context, thresholds, land disturbance, emissions, protected areas, and cumulative impacts under Environmental Code Articles R.122-2 and related tables. An ICPE permit or registration process may also require an environmental assessment or public consultation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the applicable ICPE order, prefectural permit or registration requirements, Environmental Code water-discharge rules, EU air-quality and industrial-emissions requirements where applicable, and airport environmental constraints. Control particulate matter, dust, VOCs, odours, combustion emissions, runoff, hydrocarbon contamination, and noise. Store bitumen, fuels, and hazardous substances in contained areas; classify and track wastes; use licensed waste carriers and facilities. Numerical limits are set by the applicable permit, standardized ministerial order, or site-specific authorization and must not be exceeded.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain airport operator approval, airside access permits, work permits, foreign-object-debris controls, vehicle and radio authorizations, and any DGAC or aerodrome safety clearances required by the contract. Obtain fire-safety review for buildings, fuel, bitumen, and plant installations from the competent local fire and rescue service where required. Verify structural load capacity for heavy paving equipment, temporary works, storage areas, and access routes through competent engineering inspection. Implement the French Labour Code occupational-risk assessment, single risk-assessment document, site coordination plan, worker training, personal protective equipment, hot-work controls, traffic separation, emergency procedures, chemical-risk controls, and required occupational-health arrangements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — national tax administration; professional portal: impots.gouv.fr (Espace Professionnel / EDI-TVA reporting); customs and indirect tax authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) — portal: douane.gouv.fr; business registration single window: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned French SAS: (1) file articles of association and register the entity on formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr to obtain SIREN/SIRET via INSEE; (2) submit Déclaration d'existence to the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) to obtain the TVA intracommunautaire (FR + 11-digit VAT number); (3) where no permanent establishment is created, register as a non-established taxable person with the DGFiP Non-Résidents unit and, if charged with customs/export formalities, obtain an EORI number from DGDDI; (4) appoint a fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) if not established in France and VAT obligations are triggered. Standard turnaround: VAT ID issued within 2–4 weeks after registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS) is inherently subject to French corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) on worldwide profits at a 25% standard rate (15% up to €42,500 for eligible small businesses); no statutory pass-through option exists for an SAS (profits are taxed in the entity's own hands; distributions attract withholding tax subject to treaty relief); territorial scope is the worldwide income principle, with foreign permanent-establishment profits eligible for treaty-based exemption or group consolidation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not apply the US check-the-box election. Available statutory mechanisms for an SAS: (1) groupe d'intégration fiscale (French tax consolidation under CGI Art. 223A) election for 95%-owned group members; (2) election for tax transparency in limited sectors only (e.g., qualifying professional or research structures — not an ordinary SAS); (3) capital-gains rollover elections for reinvested proceeds and real-estate/REIT-type regimes for certain qualifying vehicles; (4) VAT group election (unité d'assujettissement under CGI Art. 256 C for economically integrated entities); (5) hybrid mismatch elections and notifiable filing under DAC6/ATAD rules where applicable; (6) option for the French territorial company tax regime in narrow statutory circumstances (e.g., real-estate investment vehicles).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (value added tax / VAT), implemented under Directive 2006/112/EC (French VAT Code: CGI Arts. 256 et seq.).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For established French businesses: annual turnover ceiling of €91,900 (net of VAT) for supplies of goods and €36,800 for service/construction supplies triggers mandatory VAT registration; no franchise-en-base applies on new buildings or immovable works. Non-established foreign suppliers are registrable from the first euro of French taxable activity without any threshold. For this runway-paving contract (services connected with French immovable property), VAT registration is mandatory irrespective of turnover from the commencement of works in France.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates structured electronic invoicing in a phased rollout: from 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and from 1 September 2027 for all sectors. Domestic B2B invoices must be transmitted via the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF / Chorus Pro) or through accredited Private Dematerialisation Platforms (PDP), using the EN 16931 / Factur-X data formats with API transmission (3WS endpoints). Separate e-reporting (e-reporting) obligations apply to B2C sales and cross-border transactions. Real-time clearance and digital stamping as in other jurisdictions are not applied for construction services; the regime operates through deferred transmission of transaction data. Penalties scale from €15 per invoice (capped at €15,000 annually) up to increased sanction levels for recurrent non-compliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exonération) applies to the export of movable goods physically dispatched/transported from France to a destination outside the European Union, provided the supplier retains proof of export within 3 months (or an extended 12-month period in approved cases) and records the departure in customs archives. Services connected with French immovable property — including airport runway surfacing and asphalt paving performed in France — are outside the export zero-rating exemption; their place of supply is France and 20% French VAT must be charged even where the contractual customer is non-resident. Intra-EU B2B supplies of goods may be zero-rated only where the customer's valid EU VAT ID is obtained and the French report (ESA) identifies the transaction. Foreign contractors performing works in France should claim refund of French input VAT via the 8th/13th Directive refund procedure rather than zero-rating of services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: French customs export declaration (Déclaration en Douane, regime EX) with customs clearance stamp/electronic validation
Bill of Lading, air waybill or CMR road consignment note evidencing movement out of the EU
Proof of physical export (delivery certificate from the carrier, destination customs entry, or Export Delivery Certificate)
Commercial invoice and full packing list
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT bank credit instruction evidencing payment of the export price from the non-EU customer
EORI validation report and Intrastat declaration where intra-EU supplies are involved
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP and DGDDI may audit all export documentation; failure to furnish conclusive proof of export within the statutory period triggers reassessment of the excluded turnover at 20% French VAT, plus procedural penalties: 40% for insincere declarations (mauvaise foi), 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres (manoeuvre frauduleuse), regulatory interest at 0.2% per month, and possible loss of deduction rights. Customs declaration fraud is a criminal offence under Code des Douanes Art. 414/414-1 punishable by up to 3 years' imprisonment and fines up to €450,000. Clawback is retrospective to the beginning of the statutory audit window — normally 3 years, extended to 6 years for tax fraud, with no time limit where the claim is tainted by money laundering.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France and the French Foreign Exchange Administration (Direction Générale des Finances et du Contrôle des Changes, Banque de France)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is part of the euro area and operates under full current-account and capital-account convertibility pursuant to EU Treaty provisions and the French Monetary and Financial Code. Profit remittances, dividend distributions, loan repayments and reinvestable capital outflows are not subject to exchange-control approval, provided that the underlying transaction is lawful, accurately reported and supported by appropriate corporate and banking documentation. Cross-border monetary flows above statutory thresholds must be declared to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments purposes. There are no material legal impediments to profit repatriation for a French SAS executing an international airport runway asphalt paving contract.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose any mandatory surrender of export proceeds. Exporters may freely retain domestic and foreign-currency export receipts without any statutory conversion ratio or repatriation timeline. The only binding obligation is to declare cross-border transactions above the regulatory threshold pursuant to Articles L.161-7 and R.161-7 of the French Monetary and Financial Code. For an ISIC 4210 runway paving scope, all foreign receipts should therefore be remitted directly into the SAS operational account and identified with an appropriate balance-of-payments purpose code.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium and only as a complementary treasury rail. EU-licensed electronic money institutions can provide fast SEPA and SWIFT payment accounts, but they are not credit institutions and generally cannot issue or confirm commercial letters of credit, provide trade-finance escrow structures or offer committed credit lines. Offshore digital EMIs without a French or PSD2 passport are likely to be treated as high-risk counterparties by French banks and should not be used as primary capital escrow or operational clearing accounts for an international airport infrastructure project.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French banks generally allow account onboarding through enhanced remote due diligence, including video-identification and a compliance interview conducted by videoconference for the legal representative and beneficial owners. Physical attendance of directors at a bank branch is not an absolute legal mandate under the French AML framework, but may in practice be required when the proposed corporate structure is opaque, when the beneficial owner is a politically exposed person, or when the bank’s risk appetite demands in-person confirmation of signature specimens. For maximum onboarding success, the SAS should prepare both remote identification credentials and a Paris-based meeting capacity for one director or authorized signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO transparency and majority ownership by non-resident individuals or overseas holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized certificate of incorporation of the SAS, articles of association, registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (Register of Beneficial Owners), passport copies of all UBOs, proof of residential address, corporate structure chart extending to ultimate owners, companies registry extracts, and audited financial statements of the ultimate parent entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified source of funds for share capital injection and cross-border infrastructure escrow funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements from the remitting institution, notarized signature specimen for directors, sworn source-of-wealth letter, board resolution approving the capital injection, explanation of the international runway paving contract cash flow, and copies of the signed civil works agreement showing the escrow triggers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP status or ownership appearing on watchlists among counterparties, subcontractors or public clients
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening report from an independent compliance database, PEP assessment report, beneficial ownership attestation for counterparties and subcontractors, government client identification documents, public procurement award letter, and contractually bound compliance representation clauses from the airport concessionaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between corporate activity and the volume of expected cross-border trade payments for asphalt-related procurement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed airport civil-works contract, detailed invoices and purchase orders for polymer-modified bitumen, runway aggregate and placing equipment, expected payment schedule, certification from the asphalt supplier, VAT registration certificate in the operating jurisdiction, and construction phase project plan.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections to the French SAS should be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the parent entity’s bank into the SAS's dedicated capital escrow account. The wire instruction should identify the transaction as a capital contribution or share subscription, state the complete legal name of the SAS and its registration number, include the board resolution reference, and use the French balance-of-payments purpose code for foreign direct investment in capital. Cross-border incoming transfers above the reporting threshold must be reported to the Banque de France via the resident receiving bank. Supporting documentation should include the SAS statuts, share subscription agreement, proof of identity of subscribing shareholders, and the source-of-funds report.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for asphalt materials, aggregates, polymers, equipment and subcontractors should be cleared primarily through SWIFT MT103 messages for non-EUR and high-value payments, commercial documentary letters of credit opened in favor of raw-material suppliers against the presentation of commercial invoice, certificate of origin, packing list, transport document and asphalt quality certificates, and SEPA credit transfers for euro-denominated intra-EU vendor payments. For public airport concession payment collections, the SAS should maintain a dedicated euro operational account capable of receiving beneficiary-pays wire transfers and direct credit-driven payments from the civil aviation authority or its financing bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla EUR/USD and EUR/GBP foreign exchange forwards with an approved French bank or investment-grade counterparty
Non-deliverable forwards on emerging-market currencies used in cross-border materials procurement where local currency convertibility is restricted or off-balance-sheet settlement is required
Cross-currency interest rate swaps to convert floating-rate foreign-currency construction debt into fixed-rate euro liabilities
FX collar and participating forward structures to protect runway paving project margins from adverse bitumen-price and currency movements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of result
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders or other competent corporate body designated in the SAS articles
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end, unless extended by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction may compel approval; directors may incur liability. No automatic administrative strike-off solely for late approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts and required management documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registry of the competent Commercial Court through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval; two months where filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction and civil fine may apply. Failure to file may result in registry enforcement measures and, after formal procedures and prolonged inactivity, administrative removal from the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return, Form 2065 and required schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after financial year-end, or by the second business day after 1 May for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest and tax penalties generally apply, including a 10% surcharge, subject to statutory exceptions and tax-authority discretion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT annual or periodic returns and annual VAT summary where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly under the normal regime; annual CA12 filing for the simplified regime within the prescribed tax-calendar deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest and penalties generally apply, including a 10% surcharge and possible assessment based on available information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registry of the competent Commercial Court through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any change in beneficial-owner information or the control structure; no separate annual filing where information remains unchanged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction, criminal penalties for non-compliance, and possible restrictions affecting registration and access to certain corporate services.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally required where the SAS exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at financial year-end: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional rules apply to qualifying parent, subsidiary, or controlled groups. Threshold application must be confirmed for the relevant financial year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Commercial Code accounting rules and the French Accounting Standards Authority regulations; IFRS may be used for consolidated accounts where legally permitted or required, but is not generally mandatory for individual SAS statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a routine annual beneficial-owner confirmation where previously filed information remains accurate. The SAS must monitor ownership and control continuously and file an amendment within 30 days after any relevant change. Share transfers must be recorded in the share-transfer register and shareholder accounts, with related corporate approvals documented as required by the articles.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of collective decisions of shareholders or the competent corporate body
Individual shareholder accounts or equivalent ownership records
Copies of approved annual accounts and corporate decision documents
Beneficial-owner information and supporting control analysis maintained for compliance purposes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 300-1,500 per year, depending on provider, city, mail handling, and administrative services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,500-12,000 per year for a non-complex SAS; materially higher for regulated, consolidated, or operationally complex construction businesses

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on first EUR 38,125 of taxable profit for SMEs with turnover below EUR 10 million; research tax credit (CIR) and innovation tax credit (CII) available; territorial economic contribution (CET) is separate from income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (main corporate income tax return) and annexes (2058-A to 2058-G); filed electronically via the EFI (Echange de Formulaires Informatisés) portal or the professional tax online service (impots.gouv.fr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is the 3rd month following the fiscal year-end (or 4th month if filed electronically). For fiscal year ending 31 December, deadline is 3 May (or 4 May for online).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss after adjustments (reintegration of non-deductible expenses, deduction of tax credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a French permanent establishment must report French-source income; apply treaty provisions for income allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains and losses on disposal of fixed assets, subject to specific rates (e.g., 25% standard, 12.8% for long-term gains on shares).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gains from French real estate or business assets; treaty may allocate taxing rights.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (e.g., CIR, CII, foreign tax credits) to be deducted from the gross tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty relief for foreign taxes paid; attach Form 2065-SD for credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reductions for specific investments (e.g., cultural patronage, territorial investments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only applicable if the non-resident has a French PE and meets eligibility criteria.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the tax due, plus 0.5% per month of delay (capped at 10% after 12 months). Interest for late payment: 0.2% per month. Additional penalties for fraudulent filing: 40% or 80% of the tax due.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (domestic law) for dividends paid to non-resident companies; reduced to 0% or 5% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or tax treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident beneficiary must provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, submit Form 5000 (or 5001 for individuals) to the French tax administration, and apply for reduced withholding at source or request a refund. The process requires prior approval for certain treaty benefits (e.g., under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory rate 33.33% (or 30% for certain IP); treaty rates typically 0% (EU) or 5-10% (other treaties). Interest: statutory rate 30% (or 50% for non-cooperative states); treaty rates typically 0% (EU) or 10-15% (other treaties).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million (annual turnover or total assets) triggers mandatory full transfer pricing documentation (Master File and Local File). For smaller entities, a simplified documentation requirement applies if turnover exceeds EUR 50 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies the 'substance over form' principle and has a General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR). While no specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) exist, entities must demonstrate real economic activity (e.g., employees, premises, decision-making) to avoid challenges under the anti-abuse provisions and to benefit from treaty or EU directives.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income, false accounting, or concealment of profits from runway paving contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties: up to EUR 500,000 fine and 5 years imprisonment (increased to 7 years for aggravated cases). Administrative penalties: 40% to 80% of the tax evaded, plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they have committed fraud or mismanagement. Civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment (up to 5 years) are possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a French SAS with no real economic substance (no employees, no premises, no operational activity) solely to obtain tax benefits or treaty access.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, and imposition of 40% penalty for lack of substance. The company may be dissolved and directors fined up to EUR 375,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for taxes and penalties if they knowingly used the entity as a sham. Travel bans and imprisonment (up to 3 years) may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the runway paving business to launder proceeds from illegal activities, e.g., through inflated invoices or cash payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties: up to EUR 750,000 fine and 10 years imprisonment. Asset forfeiture and confiscation of proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability, including imprisonment and fines. Civil liability for damages, travel bans, and prohibition from managing companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting non-arm's length prices for cross-border transactions (e.g., overpaying for asphalt materials from related parties) to shift profits out of France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, 40% penalty for lack of documentation, and interest. If deemed a sham, 80% penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the tax adjustment if they knowingly participated in the manipulation. Civil penalties and potential criminal charges for tax fraud.
